The full set of keys and the lock's data sheet were handed over; the old lock or cylinder was returned to the client
The door, frame and surrounding finishes have no damage beyond what was agreed before the work started ("before" and "after" photos)
After the opening, a working lock or cylinder was fitted: it turns through every turn with every key
The opened mechanism was handed to the client and the paperwork for the job (record or receipt) was completed
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.electrical: "Before" photos of the room and of the old wiring and consumer unit were uploaded to the agreement before the start
The chases and holes were made good, the dust from chasing was cleared, and the waste was bagged
Finishes and property outside the work area have no new damage — compared with the "before" photos
What was done matches the specification and the addenda; work outside the agreed scope is not billed
The client's leftover cable and materials were counted and handed back, and the accessories that were removed were returned
Every light fitting switches on with its own circuit; two-way and intermediate switches work from each position
The fittings are mounted with no play and sit on the setting-out — the distances from the walls and centre lines match the plan (tape measure)
Dimmable fittings dim without flicker or buzzing at minimum brightness
Pendants and track lights do not swing when pressed lightly by hand — they are fixed into the structure, not into the finish
The accessories have no play, the faceplates sit against the wall with no gap greater than 1 mm, and banks of sockets are on one line (checked with a level)
Every socket works and grips a plug with normal force without pulling out of the wall; every switch operates its own circuit
In earthed sockets the earth contact is connected — checked with a socket tester
The back boxes are set flush: the accessory neither stands proud of the wall nor sinks into it
Every breaker is labelled, and the consumer unit schedule is fixed inside the door or handed to the client
The test button on every RCD or RCBO trips its circuit; the main switch cuts power to everything
A socket tester at 2–3 points confirms that live, neutral and earth are connected the right way round
The cables in the consumer unit are dressed, the cover closes fully, and no live parts are exposed on the outside
After 30 minutes under load, the breaker bodies and the terminals are not warm (by hand or with a non-contact thermometer)
A drawing or photo record of the concealed cable runs before plastering was handed over (with tape-measured dimensions from the corners and openings)
Every point (socket, outlet, switch) works — checked with a phone charger or a tester, working through the point list
The test button on every RCD or RCBO trips its own circuit
Every circuit is labelled at the consumer unit and was traced: switching off a breaker kills exactly its own circuit
After 30 minutes under load (kettle or heater) the sockets and breakers are not warm to the touch and there is no smell of hot plastic
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.engineerin: Defects schedule: every defect with a photo, its location and a reference to the requirement it breaches (a standard or the contract with the developer)
Instrument checks were carried out: a 2 m straightedge on the walls and floor, a level on the windows and doors, and a paper-sheet test on the ventilation — the results are in the report
The schedule was prepared for submission to the developer (signed or sent) and the client has a copy
The result was handed over as files through the agreement on the platform (not only in a messenger): PDF plus an editable format, as the agreement provides
The client's source material (documents, plans, keys to the property) was returned

The quantities match the survey — 2–3 lines spot-checked with a tape measure on site
Labour, materials and contingency are shown separately; the unit rates allow the estimate to be recalculated if the quantities change
The survey drawing covers every room with linear dimensions, heights and the positions of the openings
3 random dimensions spot-checked with a tape measure — the difference is no more than 10 mm
The areas are calculated room by room and in total; the drawing was handed over in an editable format and as PDF (as the agreement provides)
The design includes the set needed for approval: "before/after" plans with dimensions, a room schedule and detail drawings — per the sheet list
The design was produced by a provider holding the accreditation or qualification that local rules require for design work — the supporting document is attached
The dimensions on the drawings match the actual space — 3 dimensions spot-checked with a tape measure (difference no more than 10 mm)
Each stage is covered by a written report with photos; every finding cites the specific requirement it breaches (a standard or a term of the agreement)
The records for concealed work were signed before it was closed in (wiring, pipes, waterproofing) — the set was handed over to the client
Every finding has a recorded status showing it was put right, with a follow-up photo
"Before" photos of the surfaces to be finished were taken and uploaded to the agreement before the start
The room was cleared: the waste was bagged and splashes and drips of mortar and paint were removed from the floor, windows and doors
Finishes and property outside the work area have no new damage — compared with the "before" photos
What was done matches the specification and the addenda; work outside the agreed scope is not billed
The client's leftover materials (wallpaper, paint, mixes) were counted and handed back — a reserve for matching during future repairs
The texture and pattern are even, and the joints between working sections are not visible from 1.5–2 m
The finish matches the sample panel agreed before the work started when compared side by side
There are no cracks, no lifting and no patches; the pattern is not broken at the corners and reveals
The colour is even: from 2 m in daylight there are no bands, patches, runs or roller marks

Coverage is complete: the old colour and the filler do not show through, including under raking torchlight
The wall is out of plumb by no more than 2 mm per 1 m of straightedge and no more than 10 mm over the full height of the room
Under a 2 m straightedge there are no more than 2 gentle undulations up to 3 mm deep or high per 4 m²
There are no cracks and no voids: tapping with the handle of a trowel gives a solid sound across the whole area, and the corners and reveals are square
Under raking torchlight close to the wall there are no shadows from hollows, scratches or tool marks
The gap under a 2 m straightedge is no more than 2 mm
The surface is evenly matt and does not chalk: running your palm over it leaves no dust on your hand, and there is no flaking
The joints between lengths are not visible from 1.5–2 m in daylight and the pattern is matched
There are no bubbles, creases, marks or lifting — checked by running your palm over the paper
The edges at the ceiling, skirting, sockets and reveals are trimmed straight, with no tears and no gaps
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.flooring.c: "Before" photos of the floor substrate were uploaded to the agreement before the start (for a screed — the state of the slab; for floor coverings — the screed)
The room was cleared: dust and offcuts of the covering were collected and traces of mixes removed from the floor and skirtings
The doors open over the finished floor without catching anywhere through their swing
Finishes and property outside the work area have no new damage — compared with the "before" photos
The client's leftover covering and materials were counted and handed back — a reserve for matching during future repairs
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.flooring.l: There are no gaps or steps between boards — the joints cannot be felt with your palm, and the 8–10 mm expansion gap at the walls is covered by the skirting (per the manufacturer's instructions)
The floor does not creak or flex — checked by walking over the whole area, including the corners
The surface is flat: the gap under a 2 m straightedge is no more than 2 mm, and at the doors the threshold strips have no sharp edges
The sheet has no waves, bubbles or blisters — tapping and walking over it reveals no voids
The seams are welded or butted tight: the joint is not visible from 1 m and the pattern lines up across it
The edges are tucked under the skirting or threshold strips all the way round, and the corners do not lift
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.flooring.p: The gap under a 2 m straightedge is no more than 2 mm
There is no creaking anywhere on the floor (walk it with pauses) and the boards do not move underfoot
The laying pattern matches the agreed drawing, the gaps between boards are not visible from 1 m, and there is an expansion gap at the walls under the skirting
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.flooring.s: The gap under a 2 m straightedge is no more than 2 mm under laminate, parquet or vinyl and no more than 4 mm under tiles
The deviation from horizontal is no more than 0.2% of the room's dimension (checked with a laser or spirit level)
The surface has no cracks wider than hairline and tapping gives a solid sound with no voids; the perimeter edge strip is still in place
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.flooring.u: Photos of the cable or mats and the sensor (in its conduit) being laid, taken before the pour or the covering went down, were handed over
30–60 minutes after switching on, the floor warms evenly across the whole zone (by hand or with a household thermometer) with no cold strips
The thermostat controls the floor: changing the set point switches the heating on and off, and the floor sensor shows the temperature
The underfloor heating circuit is protected by its own RCD or RCBO — the test button cuts the heating
"Before" photos (the furniture or flat pack in its packaging, its condition on receipt) were uploaded to the agreement
The packaging was collected and taken out as agreed, and the floor and walls where the assembly took place have no new damage — compared with the "before" photos
The leftover fixings, keys and instructions were handed to the client
Every door and drawer opens without sticking and the gaps between fronts are even — no more than 2 mm out
The furniture is stable and does not rock on the floor; tall cabinets and shelving units are fixed to the wall (mandatory where the fixings come with the unit)
There are no parts left over and no fixings left untightened, and the surfaces have no scratches or chips (inspected from 0.5 m)
The repair was demonstrated: the mechanism, hinge or drawer runs smoothly for at least 5 cycles in a row
The repaired joint has no play under load (sit on it, press it by hand)
The colour and texture of the restored area do not stand out from 1 m in daylight
The worktop is horizontal (the level bubble is centred along its whole length) and the joint with the wall is closed by an upstand with no gaps
The cut-outs are sealed: after 15 minutes of running water at the sink it is dry under the worktop and inside the cabinet (checked with a cloth)
The fronts are in one plane with even gaps (no more than 2 mm out), and the built-in appliances switch on and work
The fabric is stretched with no folds or wrinkles and the pattern or stripes are not skewed (inspected from 1 m on every side)
The seams and piping are straight, and the staples and fixings are neither visible nor felt where the body touches the furniture
After assembly the frame does not creak or wobble — checked by sitting on it at different points
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.groundwork: "Before" photos of the plot and the setting-out of the axes were uploaded to the agreement before the excavation started
The site was cleared: the formwork was struck and taken away or stacked, and leftover concrete and soil dealt with as agreed
The utility lines, structures and surfaces on the plot were not damaged by machinery — compared with the "before" photos
What was done matches the design and the addenda; work outside the agreed scope is not billed
There is a fall away from the house: poured water runs outwards and no puddles stand at the plinth
The surface is even (the gap under a 2 m straightedge is no more than 5 mm) and floated with no blowholes; the movement joints are cut or formed
The edges are straight with no chips; after a week there are no through cracks (hairline shrinkage cracks are acceptable)
The depth and width follow the design: spot-measured with a tape at 3 points, deviation no more than ±50 mm
The bottom is level and trimmed, with no loose material and no standing water; the sides are not collapsing
Spoil was stockpiled or removed as the agreement provides: the plot was levelled and the topsoil (where that was agreed) stockpiled separately
The heads of every pile are on one horizontal plane — no more than 10 mm apart (water level or laser, every pile measured)
The piles follow the setting-out in the design: the centres deviate by no more than 20 mm (tape along the axes) and they are vertical by level
Screw piles were not backed off (not loosened), the cavities were filled with concrete, and the heads were welded with a continuous run and painted
An installation log or photos were handed over: the depth of every pile matches the agreement
The surface is horizontal: no more than 20 mm variation across the slab, and the gap under a 2 m straightedge is no more than 5 mm
Photos were handed over showing: two layers of reinforcement at the spacing in the design, and the sub-base and waterproofing under the slab
There are no cracks wider than hairline and no blowholes with reinforcement showing; the starter bars and cast-in fixings are positioned per the plan (tape from the axes)
The slab edges are straight, and the geometry and diagonals are within a 20 mm tolerance
The top surface varies in level by no more than 20 mm along its whole length — checked with a water level or laser
The dimensions and diagonals follow the design: the diagonals differ by no more than 20 mm (tape measure)
Photos of the reinforcement before the pour were handed over: bar diameter and spacing, and the cover held by spacers
The surface has no blowholes, no exposed reinforcement and no cracks wider than hairline (inspected after striking the formwork)
The waterproofing or coating covers the whole surface in contact with the ground (photo before backfilling)
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.handyman.c: "Before" photos of the work area were uploaded to the agreement before the start
Every task on the agreed list was done — walked through the list with the client
Work outside the agreed list is not billed (extra tasks only by an addendum)
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.handyman.m: The fault was fixed and demonstrated in use (the tap does not drip over 10 minutes of watching, the door does not drop, and so on)
The work area is clean, with no new damage to finishes or furniture (compared with the "before" photos)
The materials and parts used were agreed, and the leftovers and the parts removed were handed to the client
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.handyman.s: The shelf or curtain track is horizontal — the level bubble is centred along its whole length
It carries the load: pressing by hand (10–15 kg) produces no play and no sagging, and the fixings suit the type of wall
There are no chips or cracks around the holes and the drilling dust was cleared
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.handyman.t: The TV hangs level (checked along the top edge) and does not rock when the corners are pressed lightly
The bracket is fixed into the structural wall or a backing plate with anchors and every bolt is tightened — checked by pulling on it
The cables are run in trunking or behind the wall, and the TV switches on and tilts and swivels as the bracket's data sheet allows
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.heating.bo: The first firing is recorded in a document; for a gas boiler the commissioning and the service agreement are with an organisation authorised to carry out gas work under local rules
The gas joints were checked with soapy solution — no bubbles; there is no smell of gas in the room
The boiler reaches the set temperature, the system pressure is 1–2 bar on the gauge and does not fall over 24 hours
The concentric flue or chimney assembly falls away from the boiler to the outside, the condensate drains away, and the joints show no seepage
The data sheet, the warranty card endorsed with the commissioning, and a briefing for the client were handed over and given
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.heating.ch: The passage through the floor or roof has a fire-stopping separation from combustible structures — visible on inspection, with a photo of the detail
On a test firing the smoke goes only into the flue: there are no smoke or soot traces at the joints between sections, and the cladding nearby does not get hot (hand held near it)
The junction with the roof is watertight — the detail is dry after rain
The inspection hatch and condensate trap are reachable and open
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.heating.co: "Before" photos of the connection points and pipe runs were uploaded to the agreement; concealed heating runs were photographed before they were closed in
The work area was cleared, no system water was spilled on the finishes, and installation marks were removed
Finishes and property outside the work area have no new damage — compared with the "before" photos
What was done matches the specification and the addenda; work outside the agreed scope is not billed
The equipment that was removed and the client's leftover materials were handed back
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.heating.ra: The radiator is level; clearances: at least 60 mm from the floor, at least 50 mm from the window sill, at least 25 mm from the wall
After start-up every section warms evenly (by hand or with a thermometer) and the air was bled out through the vent
After 24 hours under pressure every joint is dry — checked with a cloth
The valves and the thermostatic head open and close freely and actually change the heat output
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.heating.ve: There is draw: an A5 sheet of paper is held against the extract grille by the airflow with a window slightly open
There is no backdraught: a lighter flame or a paper strip at the grille does not lean into the room with the windows shut
The fan or unit runs in every mode with no unusual knocking, the duct joints are sealed, and the grilles are fixed square
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.house.bath: The stove and flue are separated from combustible structures by fire-stopping or shielding, and the clearances match the stove's data sheet — visible on inspection
The steam room reaches the agreed temperature within the agreed time (checked on the thermometer in the steam room)
Water test of the washroom floor: a bucket of water drains away completely and no puddles remain
After firing, there are no smoke traces at the flue joints or where it passes through the roof, and the cladding does not get hot (hand held near it)
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.house.comm: "Before" photos of the plot and the building were taken and uploaded to the agreement before the work started
The site was cleared: building waste was collected or taken away as agreed, and the materials were stacked
Structures, the fence, surfaces and plantings outside the work area have no new damage — compared with the "before" photos
What was done matches the design or specification and the addenda; work outside the agreed scope is not billed
The client's leftover materials were counted and handed back
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.house.exte: The junction with the house is watertight: after rain the joint is dry inside and out, with no seepage
The extension's floor level meets the house's within the difference set in the agreement (measured with a tape and level)
The movement joint between the extension and the house was formed and closed with a cover strip or sealant with no breaks
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.house.gara: The gates or door open and close freely, the gap round the perimeter is even, and the catch works
No puddles remain on the floor after a bucket of water is poured out (fall towards the gates or a level surface — as the agreement provides)
After rain the roof and the wall junctions are dry inside
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.house.gaze: The posts are vertical (the level bubble is centred on two faces) and the structure does not move when rocked by hand
No daylight shows through the roof from the inside; after rain the decking under the roof is dry
The timber was sanded and coated evenly with a protective treatment, with no missed spots and no runs (inspected from 1 m)
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.house.hous: Geometry: the diagonals of the shell differ by no more than 20 mm (tape measure) and the walls are vertical — no more than 10 mm out per storey
After the first rain (or a hose test) the loft and the inside faces of the walls are dry, with no seepage
Every window and door opens and closes without force and without catching, and the house locks
Photos and records of the concealed stages were handed over: foundation reinforcement, roof details, insulation
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.insulation: "Before" photos of the surfaces to be insulated were uploaded to the agreement before the start
The work area was cleared: offcuts of insulation and membranes were collected and the dust removed
Finishes and property outside the work area have no new damage — compared with the "before" photos
The client's leftover materials were counted and handed back
The construction is isolated: there are resilient pads round the perimeter and no rigid bridges to the walls or ceiling — photographed before it was boarded over
Every joint, junction and back box is sealed, with no through holes (inspected with a torch)
A check measurement with a sound-meter app at the same point before and after the work, with the same source (a speaker behind the wall at a fixed volume) — the reduction is recorded
The layer is continuous: the boards butt tight, the joints are staggered, and gaps wider than 5 mm are filled — confirmed by photos taken before it was boarded over
The thickness of the layer matches the agreement — spot-measured with a tape at 2–3 points before it was closed in
The vapour barrier on the room side is taped at every joint and junction, with no tears and no sagging
The layer was applied in 2 coats, taken at least 200 mm up the walls, with the corners and pipe penetrations reinforced with tape — each coat photographed
Flood test: 2–3 cm of water for 24 hours — it stays dry below and at the neighbours' (for a basement — the walls are dry after rain)
The layer is continuous, with no missed spots and no bubbles, inspected under a light before the final covering goes down
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.lowvoltage: Walk test: every sensor triggers and shows up in the app or on the panel
Arming and disarming work from every device (fob, keypad code, app); the alarm notification arrives on the phone
When the mains is off the system runs on its backup battery (checked by switching off the breaker for 10 minutes)

Footage is written to the archive to the agreed retention (check: find and play back a clip from yesterday and from an hour ago)
Remote viewing from the client's phone is set up and works outside the home network; the cables are run in trunking or conduit

The work area was cleared, the holes were sealed, and no cables hang loose in view
Finishes and property have no new damage — compared with the "before" photos
Default passwords were changed; the provider's accounts were deleted from the client's systems
A call from the entry panel reaches every handset and the app, with clear sound and picture and no interference
The door or gate opens from inside the flat and from the app (where that was agreed) at the first press
The panel is fixed square with no play, and the hood or seal keeps the rain out (inspected after hosing it down)
Every RJ-45 outlet was tested with a cable tester and labelled at both ends (outlet and patch panel)
The speed at the furthest outlet matches the internet plan or 1 Gbit over the cable (measured with a speed test from a laptop)
Wi-Fi has a solid signal in every agreed room (measured at the furthest point); the cables are concealed in chases or trunking with no sagging
Every scenario in the brief was demonstrated live (lighting, blinds, climate, sensors) and the client can start it from their own phone
If the internet goes down the basic functions still work: the switches control the lights locally
The system drawing, the logins and passwords, and administrator rights were handed over — the client adds and removes a device themselves at acceptance
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.plumbing.c: "Before" photos of the bathroom and the connection points were uploaded to the agreement before the start
The work area was cleared and sealant and mortar marks were removed from the fittings and the tiles
Finishes and property outside the work area have no new damage — compared with the "before" photos
What was done matches the specification and the addenda; work outside the agreed scope is not billed
The fittings that were removed and the client's leftover materials were handed back
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.plumbing.f: Hot on the left, cold on the right; the lever or valves move smoothly and do not stick
With the tap open and closed there are no drips from under the spout, the nuts or the flexi hoses — checked with a cloth after 10 minutes
The tap is fixed with no play, and the spout and the shower head swivel without catching the wall or the basin
The fitting is fixed with no rocking (checked by pushing it by hand) and the rims of the bath or basin are horizontal by level
Filling and draining work; 15 minutes after a water test every joint and junction is dry (checked with a cloth)
The junction with the wall is closed with an even bead of sealant, and water running down the wall does not get into the joint (test it with water)
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.plumbing.m: The meter responds to flow: with a tap open the impeller or the digits move, and with the taps shut they stand still
The meter's data sheet was handed to the client; the seals and the paperwork for bringing the meter into use were completed under local rules
The joints before and after the meter are dry after 24 hours in use (checked with a cloth) and the isolating valve shuts the water off completely
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.plumbing.s: Fall on the horizontal pipes: 3 cm per 1 m for ø50 mm and 2 cm per 1 m for ø110 mm — checked with a level and a tape measure
Water test from every point: a bucket of water drains away fast, with no backing up, no gurgling at the neighbouring drains and no smell
The access and rodding points are reachable, and the joints are dry after the water test (a cloth run over the sockets)
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.plumbing.w: The system stood at working pressure for 24 hours: every joint is dry when checked with a cloth, and with the taps shut the meter does not turn
The valves and the manifold are labelled (hot and cold water, which fitting each serves) and are not sealed in permanently (an access hatch or door opens)
Photos of the concealed pipework before the chases and trunking were closed were handed over
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.roofing.co: "Before" photos of the roof and facade were uploaded to the agreement; the concealed layers (battens, membrane, insulation) were photographed before they were covered
The site was cleared: offcuts, fixings and packaging were collected, and the areas where screws could have fallen were gone over with a magnet
Structures, windows, the apron and plantings have no new damage — compared with the "before" photos
What was done matches the specification and the addenda; work outside the agreed scope is not billed
The client's leftover materials were counted and handed back
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.roofing.fa: Photos of the stages were handed over: boards with no gaps greater than 2 mm (gaps filled), the plate fixings, and the mesh fully bedded into the coat
The finish coat is even: the gap under a 2 m straightedge is no more than 3 mm, and the texture is uniform with no patches and no visible joints between working sections
The junctions at the windows and the plinth have proper trims or sealant, with no cracks round the openings
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.roofing.fl: The sheets lap by at least 100 mm and the edges are rolled down — there is no lifting and there are no bubbles on inspection or under light pressure
After rain or a water test the water runs to the outlets and there are no leaks below
The junctions with the parapets and pipes are turned up the vertical face and fixed with a trim and sealant, with no gaps
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.roofing.gu: A bucket of water poured into the gutter: it all runs to the outlet and down the pipes, with no overflow over the edge and no dripping at the joints
The gutters have a visible fall to the outlets (string line or level) and there is no sagging between the brackets
The downpipes are fixed with no movement and the outlet takes the water away from the foundation (into a channel or drain), not under the apron
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.roofing.pi: The rows of covering are straight, with no waves and no lifted edges — inspected from the ground along the slopes; the fixings have washers and are not overtightened (10 screws spot-checked)
After the first rain or a hose test the roof void is dry: there are no wet patches on the membrane, the insulation or the rafters
The ridge, valleys and pipe junctions are closed with trims that show no daylight through
The snow guards and drip edges are fitted per the agreed drawing (checked against the plan)
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.roofing.si: The rows are horizontal (checked with a level) and sighting along the facade shows no waves or bulging
The panels are fixed with a gap for thermal movement: a panel moves slightly sideways by hand and the screws are not driven right home (per the manufacturer's instructions)
The corners, reveals and joints are closed with matching trims, with no gaps and no cut edges sticking out
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.tiling.com: "Before" photos of the substrate and the tile setting-out drawing were agreed and uploaded to the agreement before the start
The cut tiles follow the agreed setting-out symmetrically: the cut pieces at the edges are the same width, and the openings for sockets and pipes are cut with no chips in view
The room was cleared: leftover adhesive and grout were removed from the tiles and the floor, and the waste was bagged
Finishes and property outside the work area have no new damage — compared with the "before" photos
The client's leftover tiles and materials were counted and handed back — a reserve for matching during future repairs
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.tiling.flo: The gap under a 2 m straightedge is no more than 4 mm and the step between adjacent tiles is no more than 1 mm
In the shower and around the gully, poured water runs fully to the gully and no puddles remain; in the rooms the floor is flat with no fall (a ball does not roll)
There are no voids under the tiles when tapped; the cuts at the walls and pipe penetrations are covered by skirting or collars with no chips in view
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.tiling.gro: The joints are filled to full depth, with no missed spots, cracks or pinholes (run a finger or a plastic card along them)
The grout colour is even once dry, with no patches and no efflorescence, and the tiles were washed clean of residue
The junctions with the bath, shower tray or worktop are closed with an even bead of sanitary sealant; water poured onto the joint does not get underneath
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.tiling.mos: The sheet grid does not read: the joints between sheets are the same as the joints inside a sheet (inspected from 1–1.5 m)
On flat and curved areas there are no steps between chips greater than 1 mm (run your palm over them)
No adhesive squeezes out of the joints, the grout is continuous, and the chips have no chips or marks
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.tiling.wal: The tiling is out of plumb by no more than 1.5 mm per 1 m and the gap under a 2 m straightedge is no more than 2 mm
The step between the edges of adjacent tiles is no more than 1 mm and the joint width is uniform — no more than ±0.5 mm out
There are no voids: tapping with a knuckle or a handle gives a solid sound across the whole area, especially at the corners and tile edges
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.turnkey.ap: The finished wall surfaces are flat: the gap between a 2 m straightedge and the wall is no more than 2 mm, and the wall is out of plumb by no more than 2 mm per 1 m
Walk-through against the checklist: every socket, switch, light fitting, tap and drain was switched on or run and works; the test button on the RCD trips its circuit
A photo report and drawings of the concealed work (cable runs, pipework, waterproofing), taken before it was covered by the finishes, were handed over
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.turnkey.ba: The floor waterproofing was taken at least 200 mm up the walls — confirmed by photos taken before the tiling went down
Tiling: the gap under a 2 m straightedge is no more than 2 mm, the step between adjacent tiles is no more than 1 mm, and the joints are of uniform width
Water test at every point: the water drains without backing up, the joints are dry when checked with a cloth, and a sheet of paper is held against the extract grille
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.turnkey.co: "Before" photos (every room in the work area) were taken and uploaded to the agreement before the start
The work area was cleared: building waste was bagged or taken out, and the tools and protective sheeting removed
Finishes and property outside the work area have no new damage — compared with the "before" photos
What was done matches the specification and the addenda; work outside the agreed scope is not billed
The client's leftover materials were counted and handed back, and what was removed was returned or taken away as agreed
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.turnkey.ki: The worktop is horizontal (the level bubble is centred along its whole length) and the splashback has no steps between tiles greater than 1 mm
The sink, dishwasher and hob are connected and work; after 15 minutes of running water it is dry under the sink (checked with a cloth)
Running the kettle and the oven together does not trip the breaker; the extractor or ventilation duct holds a sheet of paper against it
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.turnkey.of: The finishes are within tolerance: the gap under a 2 m straightedge is no more than 2 mm on the walls and the floor
Every system works, checked against the walk-through list: lighting, socket circuits, network outlets (tested with a cable tester), ventilation
The as-built drawings, the circuit labelling in the consumer unit and the records of concealed work were handed over
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.turnkey.ro: The walls and ceiling have no hollows or humps: the gap under a 2 m straightedge is no more than 2 mm, and raking torchlight casts no shadows from unevenness
The junctions have no gaps: the skirtings, architraves and joints between coverings have no gaps greater than 1 mm when viewed from 1 m
Every socket, switch and light fitting in the room works (checked with a phone charger and by operating each switch)
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.welding.ca: The frame does not move when rocked by hand and the posts are vertical by level
After rain it is dry under the canopy and the water runs off to the intended side, not onto the entrance or the path
The sheeting fixings have washers, and the sheets have no dents and no unfixed corners (they do not rattle in the wind)
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.welding.co: "Before" photos of the installation spot and the agreed sketch or drawing were uploaded to the agreement before the start
The site was cleared: scale, metal offcuts and weld spatter were collected, and there are no paint marks on the surfaces
Surfaces, structures and property nearby have no new damage and no burn marks — compared with the "before" photos
What was done matches the specification and the addenda; work outside the agreed scope is not billed
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.welding.ga: The leaves open and close one-handed without catching, and the gap to the ground and between the leaves is even across the full width
The lock, bolt and automation operate from every position; a leaf left half open does not move by itself
The welds are continuous, dressed and painted, with no spatter and no paint runs (inspected from 0.5 m)
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.welding.me: The geometry follows the drawing: the dimensions and diagonals are within ±3 mm per metre (tape measure)
Every weld on the load-bearing joints is continuous, dressed and primed or painted, including the underside and hidden faces (inspected with a mirror or photographed)
The structure has no play at the joints when loaded by hand; the anchors are tightened and the plates sit flush with no gap
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.welding.ra: The railing does not move when pushed with your full weight in the middle of a span and at the corners
The posts are vertical (checked with a level) and the top line is straight — no steps and no waves when sighted along it
The welds are dressed and there are no sharp edges (run your palm over them); the coating has no missed spots and no rust marks
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.windows.ba: Every casement or sliding section runs its full length without sticking, and the locks and catches hold
After rain the sill, the flashing and the joints between the frame and the parapet are dry inside, and the flashing does not rattle in the wind
The frames are level (no more than 1.5 mm out per 1 m) and the perimeter joints are filled and covered all the way round
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.windows.co: "Before" photos of the openings and the old units were uploaded to the agreement before they were taken out
The room was cleared: the foam was trimmed back, the protective film was taken off the profile, and the glass was cleaned of installation marks
The reveals, wallpaper and finishes around the opening have no new damage — compared with the "before" photos
The product data sheets and warranty cards were handed over; the items supplied (handles, caps, insect screens) match the agreement
checklists.catalog.checklists.renovation.windows.wi: The frame is plumb: no more than 1.5 mm out per 1 m, and no more than 3 mm over the height of the unit
The casements open and close without force and without catching; a sheet of paper shut in a closed casement cannot be pulled out at any point round the perimeter
The installation joint is protected: the foam is not left exposed — vapour barrier or plaster on the inside, tape or a cover strip outside, with no breaks
The repair was demonstrated: the casement does not catch the frame and does not let draughts through (a sheet of paper cannot be pulled out anywhere round the perimeter)
The handle moves smoothly into every position, and the vent and trickle-vent settings work
The new glazing unit has no chips, scratches or condensation inside the cavities; the beads sit tight with no gaps
